_comment: THE AUTHORIZED SKIPS. This file is PERMISSION, not a hint: a test that the measured suite reported with a
`# SKIP` directive makes the receipt INADMISSIBLE AS A PIN unless its exact name appears below. Nothing
else tolerates a skip - not a count, not a comment, not the fact that the skipped test sits outside the
claim's named set - and no other exclusion is tolerable at all: a failing test, a cancelled test, a `todo`
and every unmodelled exclusion the receipt records (`misplaced`, `unbound`, `unclaimed`, ...) are refusals
with no allow-list of their own. The rule that reads this file is .github/verifier-receipt/admissibility.mjs.
SHAPE. `authorized` is an array of objects, each of which must carry all three of:
test          - the test's name EXACTLY as the runner reports it, matched literally, no patterns
reason        - why this skip is ENVIRONMENTAL rather than a result: what the environment lacks, and why
a run without it still measures what the claim describes
authorized_by - who decided that, by name. An entry nobody signed authorizes nothing.
An entry missing any of the three makes the whole list unreadable to the rule, which refuses rather than
guesses; so does a file that is not valid JSON, or one that carries no `authorized` array.
IT SHIPS EMPTY BECAUSE NOTHING IS AUTHORIZED YET. Adding a name here widens what may be pinned, so an edit
to this file is an edit to the admission rule itself - it lives in the protected authority directory, and
the consumer checks its git blob id against refs/heads/main for the same reason it checks the rule's.
